fields.description:
The orphan reconciler measures staleness against a column that never advances, so it reclaims executions that are still working.

persist_execution_state upserts with on_conflict_do_update and an explicit set_ mapping that omits updated_at. SQLAlchemy fires the column's onupdate default only for UPDATE constructs, not for the set_ mapping of ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, so updated_at freezes at row creation. The reconciler grace window therefore measures age since row creation rather than age since activity. Any run that lives longer than the grace is eligible for reclamation from the moment its workflow stops being observed as live, regardless of how recently it did work.

Observed on execution intake-ee0f760a, whose frozen updated_at was thirty nine minutes old when the reconciler evaluated it thirty three seconds after its last state write, against a grace of one hundred and twenty seconds.

The reclamation audit reason also records only the workflow id, so an operator reading the audit trail cannot tell which stage a reclaimed run was in. Carrying the execution state through to the reason makes reclamations diagnosable.

Scope is limited to the freshness defect and the audit reason. Two further defects found during this investigation are tracked separately. The pull request path that does not await close never persists a terminal execution state, so a finished run keeps a concurrency slot. Intake deduplication is keyed on a ticket content digest that the platform's own write-backs mutate.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The execution upsert refreshes updated_at on conflict, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_persistence.py -k upsert_refreshes_updated_at`
- [ ] The active execution query selects the state column, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_persistence.py -k active_query_selects_state`
- [ ] A null state column maps to an empty string rather than failing, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_persistence.py -k tolerates_null_state`
- [ ] The reclamation reason records the state the run was reclaimed from, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_reconciler.py -k orphan_reason_carries_state`
- [ ] A reclamation reason for an unknown state reads as unknown, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_reconciler.py -k orphan_reason_marks_unknown_state`
- [ ] A dead execution in a working state is still reclaimed, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_reconciler.py -k reclaims_dead_working_state`
- [ ] An execution inside the grace window is left alone whatever its state, proven by `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_reconciler.py -k honours_grace_for_any_state`

## Testing
Run `pytest tests/unit/test_execution_persistence.py tests/unit/test_execution_reconciler.py -q` to prove the upsert contract and the reclamation policy, then `ruff check .` for lint.
